is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on the malaria vector Anopheles stephensi (page 1, title and abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The authors perform genome assembly and gene annotation, identifying gene families (such as kdr, rdl, ace-1), but do not genotype any specific target resistance markers (e.g., Vgsc L995F/S, Ace-1 G280S, etc.).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No population-level genotype or allele counts/frequencies of target insecticide-resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The study only sequenced a laboratory strain, UCISS2018, originally derived from the Indian subcontinent and maintained in an insectary (page 9, 'Materials and methods - Mosquitoes'). No African field samples were analyzed.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article reporting a de novo chromosome-level reference genome assembly.

sub_country_location.evidence: No African field collection sites are included; the lab strain originated from the Indian subcontinent.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection dates are reported for field populations.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable as this is a reference genome assembly paper using a specific laboratory colony.

supplement.evidence: The study does not contain target marker frequency data in supplementary files either.

assessment.summary: This study presents a de novo chromosome-level reference genome assembly and Iso-Seq transcriptome annotation of an Anopheles stephensi laboratory strain (UCISS2018) from the Indian subcontinent. It does not evaluate African field populations nor genotype any specific target insecticide resistance markers.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report any target resistance markers
Does not report extractable genotype data
Does not study African field populations (uses a laboratory colony of Indian origin)
